newsitem.title: USA: Vishay to buy 65 pct of Taiwan diode maker.
newsitem.headline: Vishay to buy 65 pct of Taiwan diode maker.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology Inc said Friday it had agreed to buy 65 percent of Lite-On Power Semiconductor Corp of Taiwan for $130 million.
The deal, which includes the purchase of 1.6 million warrants exercisable at $23 per share, is expected to close in mid-summer, it said.
Lite-On is a producer of diodes and a member of Lite-On Group of China, it said.

"We believe (Lite-On Power) is well-positioned as a low-cost producer to effect substantial market penetration as evidenced by sales in 1996 of $50.3 million, an approximate 41 (percent) increase over 1995 despite the major market decline in 1996," it said. "In the first quarter of 1997, sales were approximately $20 million, reflecting an approximate 86 (percent) sales increase as compared to the same period last year."

Vishay said the purchase was its first step into the discrete semiconductor market, which includes diodes and transistors of many types. "Vishay intends to further penetrate this market through continued acquisitions and internal growth," it said, adding that it plans to expand in Europe and Asia.

Diodes are discrete semiconductor components used to convert electrical currents from AC to DC. Applications for the products cover a range of markets including computers, telecommunications, automotive, industrial and consumer goods.
Based in Malvern, Pa., Vishay makes passive electronic components.
